comments:
Hey there @StevenLooman, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`upnp`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L438) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Thank you for the report, you've already done lots of work by investigating the traffic logging. Some devices don't provide traffic counters.

The previous work-around was lost after the rewrite, as you've noted. Again, thank you for the investigation you've already done!

I hope to fix this somewhere tomorrow.

I'm undecided if sensor value = "unknown" is the best outcome...
If a device never provides traffic counter values, should traffic sensor entities be created for it?

The [IGD/WANCommonInterfaceConfig Specs](http://upnp.org/specs/gw/UPnP-gw-WANCommonInterfaceConfig-v1-Service.pdf) state that the Actions to retrieve the traffic counters are options, see the table on page 11.

If the device does not provide any traffic counters, and thus no sensors should be created, the integration - in this case - has no use. The port forwarding was removed due to potential security problems and to slim down this integration.

What do you think @jm493, should the integration not create any sensors in this case? It will probably confuse the user if any integration is detected in this case as s/he will not see anything other than a device.

Ignoring the detected device is possible, but requires some work to decide if the device is capable of providing traffic counters.

I agree that it is better to show some (empty) sensors so as not confuse the user.

Scope creep question: can HA poll something like the "PhysicalLinkStatus" or UPnP-gw-WANIPConnection-v2-Service / upnpWANPPPConnection.xml "ConnectionStatus" as an overall device-is-working status indicator?
[ I don't have a good idea of which devices support which variables, or how to tell. ]

review_comments:
Do you specifically need to compare against `None`? If not, this is shorter:

```python
if not value:
  return None
```

Yes. `0` and `0.0` are valid values for this and the sensors below, respectivly. These sensors are counters which wrap around after 2^31-1 bytes. Although the value 0/0.0 is unlikely, certainly possible.
